ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct risk-based enhanced screening of every natural person directly or indirectly owning 25% or more and each individual exercising effective control through voting rights, board appointment, financing arrangements or family relationships, using PBOC Beneficial Owner registry filings, SAMR equity-chain data and Taiwan MOEA corporate records. Cross-reference against OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU and UK consolidated targets, PRC Ministry of Public Security terrorist organization list, Taiwan FIA/AML alerts, the World Bank debarment list, and adverse media. Use fuzzy matching, alias and prior-name detection, PEP status verification, source-of-wealth checks, and daily or event-driven re-screening. Heightened due diligence applies because semiconductor wholesale has dual-use/export-control exposure and the payment rails are SWIFT TT and escrow-inspection wires.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, Articles 8, 15, 18, 128 through 161, and 387, together with the Regulations for Company Registration and the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, Taiwan Company Registration One-Stop Service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Application Form together with Notarized Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under the Taiwan Company Act, no statutory minimum paid-up capital is required, but the subscribed capital must be fully paid into a temporarily blocked escrow bank account opened in the prospective company name, verified by a licensed Taiwan CPA, and released only after the MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate. In administrative practice, the Investment Commission expects a paid-in capital of at least NT$500,000 for a wholesale trading entity, and the escrow mechanism prevents early withdrawal of funds before legal formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY] LIMITED

At a meeting of the Board of Directors of [Company] Limited (the 'Company') duly convened and held on ______ at the registered office of the Company, the directors having waived formal notice and being present in person, and a quorum having been duly established, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded, and unanimously adopted.

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND VERIFICATION: RESOLVED, that the initial authorized and subscribed share capital of the Company is New Taiwan Dollars ______, divided into ______ ordinary shares with a par value of NT$10 per share, fully subscribed and paid in by the sole shareholder. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the funds representing such share capital are lawfully deposited in a temporary escrow bank account established in the name of the Company with [Bank Name], and that, upon receipt of the Company Registration Certificate issued by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, the escrow bank shall automatically release the funds into the Company's general operating account for lawful corporate purposes.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that [Bank Name] is designated as the principal deposit and clearing bank of the Company. RESOLVED, that the Chairperson and the General Manager, acting jointly, are authorized to open, operate, and close bank accounts, to endorse and deposit negotiable instruments, to make and receive wire transfers, to issue foreign exchange settlement instructions, and to execute any related banking agreements, security documents, and margin facilities for the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER, that any bank instruction or cheque exceeding NT$1,000,000 shall require the joint signatures of the Chairperson and the General Manager, or the General Manager and the Finance Controller.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [Registered Office Address], Taiwan, and that the Company Secretary is directed to install the Company's identification plate at that location, to maintain the statutory books and corporate seal, and to notify the Ministry of Economic Affairs and relevant tax authorities of the registered office address. RESOLVED, that the Company may move the registered office at a future date upon a resolution of the Board and a filing with the Company Registry.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed to the offices indicated, each having signified consent, with tenure until the next annual general meeting: [Name] as Chairperson; [Name] as General Manager; [Name] as Finance Controller; and [Name] as Company Secretary. RESOLVED, that the Chairperson is empowered to convene meetings of the Board and shareholders, the General Manager is empowered to conduct day-to-day business, and the Finance Controller is empowered to maintain accounting records and control the corporate bank accounts.

5. IMPLEMENTATION AND RATIFICATION: RESOLVED, that the officers and any one of them acting jointly with the corporate counsel are hereby authorized, jointly and severally, to execute, notarize, authenticate, file, and submit all applications, declarations, statements, consents, and other documentation necessary to obtain the Company Registration Certificate, tax registrations, trading registrations, and any required operating permits. RESOLVED, that all acts taken by the founders and promoters before this meeting in connection with the formation of the Company are hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved. RESOLVED, that this resolution shall remain in force until amended or revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation, Business Scope Coding, and Articles of Incorporation Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) One-Stop Company Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign promotor must log into the One-Stop Corporate Registration Portal with an MOEA-accredited electronic certificate or a notarized foreign passport. The proposed English and Chinese company names, plus the Taiwan Standard Industrial Classification code equivalent to ISIC 4651 for wholesale of computers and electronic components, must be inserted in the name reservation form. The MOEA database screens conflicting names and prohibits generic or misleading terms. Simultaneously, the promoters must execute the Articles of Incorporation, define the business scope to include wholesale brokerage of SSDs and server processors, and appoint a local corporate agent if the foreign shareholder is not resident in Taiwan. After MOEA approves the name, it remains reserved for six months, during which the capital escrow bank account and the investment approval must be completed.
required_dossiers: Completed company name search and reservation form
Articles of Incorporation in English and Chinese
Certified copy of foreign shareholder passport
Power of attorney appointing the local formation agent
Proposed business scope classification (ISIC 4651 / Taiwan Standard Classification 4641)
Proof of identity for directors and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA rejects the proposed name because of resemblance to an existing trademark or company name, the applicant may resubmit a corrected name application through the One-Stop Portal within the response window; no new fee is required if the reservation fee was already paid. Should the rejection cite incomplete business scope codes, amend the scope text and upload a revised Articles draft.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval, Bank Escrow, and Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and a licensed Taiwanese commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign shareholder must file an Application for Investment by Foreign Nationals with the Investment Commission, disclosing the direct shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, funding source, and intended business plan. After approval, the company's representative opens a temporary escrow account under the company's proposed legal name at a commercial bank in Taiwan, remits the subscribed capital by international wire, and obtains a bank deposit certificate. A licensed Taiwan CPA issues a capital verification report confirming that the capital is fully subscribed, lawfully remitted, and locked in the escrow account. The funds are blocked from operational use until the Company Registration Certificate is delivered. If the shareholder is a Hong Kong or Macau entity, the approval path is identical but subject to an additional cross-strait declaration.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission approval letter
Bank escrow account application form
Remittance slip and SWIFT proof
Capital verification report signed by Taiwan CPA
Depositor source-of-funds declaration
Company articles and power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission suspends the investment approval pending further evidence of source of funds or beneficial ownership, the promoter should submit the requested bank reference letters and an enhanced source-of-wealth declaration within 14 days. If the selected bank refuses the escrow account on AML grounds, the company may apply at a second commercial bank with a substantiated commercial plan and local compliance counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration Filing and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Central Region Company Registration Bureau (or the local branch with jurisdiction over the registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the name is reserved, the investment approval is secured, and the capital verification report is signed, the authorized agent must submit the full incorporation dossier through the One-Stop Portal. The filing must include the notarized Articles, the bank escrow confirmation, the capital report, the First Board Resolution, registered-office consent, and identification of each officer. The MOEA will assign a tax number and, after a legal compliance review, issue the Company Registration Certificate. The company must pay the official registration fee online, and any correction requests from the examiner must be answered in the portal within fifteen calendar days. The certificate is the controlling evidence of the WFOE's legal existence and is required for all later tax, customs, and bank operations.
required_dossiers: MOEA incorporation application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital verification report
Registered office consent or lease
First Board Resolution
Resident agent or officer consent forms
Tax due diligence declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a correction notice, the applicant has 15 calendar days to cure all remarks through the online portal. If the registration is refused after two correction cycles, the company may file a written administrative appeal with the MOEA Commercial Affairs Department within 30 days of the refusal decision, annexing the original application package and the reasons for the appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Uniform Invoice, Import-Export Filing, and Business Premises Endorsement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Foreign Trade; local municipal government and Fire Bureau (only if warehousing is used)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fifteen days of receiving the Company Registration Certificate, the company must apply to the National Taxation Bureau for a profit-seeking enterprise uniform invoice number and for a withholding tax file for employees and contractors. For the wholesale import and export of SSD and CPU chips, the company must also register as an exporter and importer with the Bureau of Foreign Trade, obtain a customs registration code, and endorse the applicable business tax and tariff classifications. If the company decides to store inventory in any Taiwan physical warehouse, the business, warehouse use, and fire safety approvals must be obtained from the municipal Public Works and Fire Departments before inventory is received. This step finalizes the company's tax, customs, and municipal profile and allows execution of Swift TT and escrow-inspection wire rails.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Uniform invoice application form
Photocopy of registered office lease and business license
Import and export registration application and customs forms (if applicable)
Warehouse fire safety inspection request (if applicable)
Taxpayer withholding application and company chop impression
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Taxation Bureau questions the uniform invoice application because of incomplete address or owner consent, the company should submit the missing notarized lease or owner consent within the statutory response period. If a fire safety inspection fails, the company should abate all cited hazards and request a re-inspection by the municipal Fire Department; operations involving inventory storage must remain suspended until the permit is granted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Bureau of Foreign Trade (trade-level oversight only; no industrial license for pure wholesale brokerage). Municipal Fire and Public Works Bureaus would only be engaged in the event of future warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no sector-specific operating license for open-market wholesale brokerage of SSDs and server processors under Taiwan law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - full EIA report not required because the primary activity is wholesale brokerage (ISIC 4651), not manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or regulated warehousing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no process wastewater, volatile organic compound (VOC), hazardous waste, or stationary emission sources are generated. If the future business adds a warehouse of more than 2,000 square meters, an Environmental Registration may be triggered; otherwise, general waste handling contracts under the Waste Disposal Act are sufficient.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for pure brokerage activity. Should any physical auxiliary storage be operated, the company must obtain a small-scale warehouse fire safety inspection certificate from the local Fire Department, a structural load and building use compliance certificate from the Public Works Authority, and an occupational exposure assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act before occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (国家税务总局), electronic filing and registration through the Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax Portal) at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn. Where applicable to cross-strait trade with Taiwan, the Taiwan competent authority remains the National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance for Taiwanese counterparty obligations, but the Chinese WFOE is exclusively registered with the State Taxation Administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The WFOE must first obtain a Unified Social Credit Code from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System. Tax registration is then completed automatically under the 'one code, one license' system, but the WFOE must complete taxpayer qualification filing through the Electronic Tax Administration portal or in person with the competent local tax bureau. The foreign parent must provide notarized and legalized incorporation documents, passport or corporate identity documents, the WFOE's approved articles of association, business license, ownership or lease documentation for the registered address, bank account information, and identification of the legal representative, financial officer, and tax agent. The WFOE must elect VAT registration status; because it will engage in wholesale exports and require input VAT credits, it should apply for General VAT Taxpayer status by submitting accounting system documentation and projected turnover. It must also register for the electronic fiscal invoice system, obtain a tax electronic UKey or fiscal digital certificate, and enroll with the General Administration of Customs under the customs registration number for export declarations and export VAT refund/rebate procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide check-the-box or other hybrid entity elections for WFOEs. The entity is a resident enterprise for Corporate Income Tax purposes. VAT General Taxpayer versus Small-Scale Taxpayer classification is determined by annual taxable turnover thresholds, not an elective hybrid regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the People's Republic of China VAT Law and its implementing regulations, administered by the State Taxation Administration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Registration as a VAT taxpayer is mandatory upon issuing a business license. The mandatory threshold for classification as a General VAT Taxpayer is annual VAT taxable turnover exceeding RMB 5,000,000. Below that threshold, the entity is a Small-Scale VAT Taxpayer unless voluntary General VAT Taxpayer registration is approved. For export trading of SSD and CPU chips, the WFOE should be registered as a General VAT Taxpayer to access 0% export zero rating and input VAT refund rights.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the issuance of electronic invoices through the State Taxation Administration's unified Electronic Invoice Service Platform and the fully digitalized electronic invoice system. VAT special invoices and ordinary invoices must be issued using the national tax-controlled system with real-time data transmission. The transaction data, invoice number, amount, VAT rate, and taxpayer identification are cleared and verified through the STA's digital anti-fraud stamping and invoice verification system; the system assigns a unique invoice code and streams the fiscal data to the tax authority in near real time. No private or non-official invoicing software may issue legally valid VAT invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A General VAT Taxpayer exporting goods out of the customs territory of the People's Republic of China is eligible for a 0% VAT rate on the export sales. For the WFOE's wholesale trade of solid-state drives and server processors to Taiwan or any other jurisdiction, the goods must physically leave China through a formal customs export declaration; the seller must retain evidence of the export customs declaration, transport movement, and receipt of foreign currency or settlement in accordance with State Administration of Foreign Exchange rules. The export sales proceeds must be repatriated into China through designated foreign exchange channels or justified under the SAFE trade settlement records. The export zero-rating applies to the merchandise sold if the WFOE is the exporter of record and all statutory documentation is complete. Concurrently, the WFOE may claim refund or credit for input VAT embedded in purchases of goods and services used in the export trade.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单) issued by the General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical shipment from a Chinese customs port to the Taiwan destination or other foreign destination
Commercial Invoice issued by the WFOE to the overseas purchaser, clearly stating the export goods, unit prices, total price, and 0% VAT treatment
Packing List matching the commercial invoice and customs declaration
Export Contract or Purchase Order between the WFOE and the overseas buyer
Foreign Exchange Loan/Proceeds Collection Certificate or Bank Receipt issued by a Chinese designated bank evidencing receipt of export payment through lawful cross-border settlement channels
Customs clearance release notice and customs tax payment or exemption documents, if applicable
Export VAT refund declaration and related STA export tax rebate filing evidence (submitted via the electronic tax system after customs export data cross-matches)
Transportation documents, including forwarders' cargo receipt or carrier certificate where a multimodal move is used
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to strict post-clearance audits by the State Taxation Administration and the General Administration of Customs. If the WFOE fails to substantiate the physical export, misdeclares the HS classification, or does not repatriate export proceeds within the foreign exchange regulatory deadline, the 0% VAT treatment is reversed. The tax authority will assess output VAT at 13% retroactively, impose a daily late payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax, and may impose administrative fines from 50% to five times the amount of tax evaded. Fraudulent export tax refund behavior can result in refusal of refunds, revocation of export tax rebate eligibility, and criminal liability under the Criminal Law for the legal representative. Customs penalties and the collection of unverified VAT amounts may compound with civil clawback and foreign-exchange penalties under SAFE regulations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed dual-account foreign exchange convertibility system. Current account transactions, representing cross-border goods trade in SSD and CPU chips with Taiwan, are broadly convertible through designated domestic banks after genuine-trade verification. The WFOE may receive export proceeds in USD or RMB and can pay imports using the retained foreign currency, provided the customs and SAFE trade verification data base matches invoice, shipping, and contract documents. On the capital account side, convertibility is restricted and controlled: foreign equity injections from the Taiwanese parent must be registered with SAFE under the Foreign Direct Investment negative list, booked as an equity investment or external debt, and converted via a formal foreign exchange capital account. Profit remittance from the WFOE to the Taiwan shareholder is a capital item and requires a post-audit distributable profit, a tax clearance from the Chinese State Taxation Administration, and proof of reserve allocation; dividends are freely remittable thereafter but subject to 10% corporate income tax withholding in the absence of a cross-strait tax treaty, and full disclosure of the ultimate beneficial owner is demanded. Since 2012, SAFE has removed compulsory surrender of export proceeds, but the funds must be repatriated within the statutory documentary reconciliation period and cannot remain offshore without a special trade-plant reason. In practice, frequent regulatory barriers arise where the authenticity of the underlying trade or the final destination of the semiconductor goods is unclear; banks will apply strict trade-based anti-money-laundering checks and may reject or suspend any remittance that lacks a complete chain of evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: As of the current SAFE centralised trade settlement regime, there is no statutory mandate to convert all export proceeds into RMB; the enterprise may elect to retain foreign exchange in its foreign exchange settlement account or convert it at will. However, export proceeds must be repatriated into China through the designated bank and be verified against the customs export declaration within the usual 90-calendar-day trade term (extendable under documentary credit or consignment arrangements). Any proceeds not repatriated within the agreed payment term must be justified to SAFE and, if necessary, the enterprise must apply for a foreign exchange delay filing. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero; the only requirement is that conversion, if made, must be in the name of the WFOE and must be reported under the actual trade purpose code.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (RMB current account) plus Foreign Exchange Capital Account for equity injection

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FX capital account) and Corporate Free Trade Account (FTE)
Basic RMB Deposit and Withdrawal Account plus Forex Settlement Account
RMB general corporate account and foreign currency settlement account
Designated Foreign Exchange Bank Account under SAFE registration

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Foreign fintech EMIs, including Hong Kong-licensed SMEs and Europe-based digital banks such as Airwallex or Currenxie, are not allowed to open domestic RMB or foreign currency settlement accounts for Chinese WFOEs without an approved payment institution licence from the People's Bank of China and the CBIRC. They can only act as unlicensed foreign payment service providers facilitating collection outside mainland China; they cannot channel imported capital, verify trade declarations, or process RMB-clearing payments inside China. Consequently, the formation treasury should treat EMIs as low-viability alternatives for the WFOE's actual account structure. If the corporate treasury seeks to support non-residential expense accounts for the Taiwan parent or overseas vendors, an EMI is permissible only for external FX deposits and must be backed by a regulated MSB licence in the relevant overseas jurisdiction; it still cannot replace a domestic Tier-1 bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the PBoC account opening and anti-money laundering regulations, the statutory legal representative or an appointed local manager with a board-authorised power of attorney must attend a physical in-branch interview at the designated Tier-1 bank when opening both the basic RMB account and the foreign exchange capital account. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted in mainland China. The bank will verify the business license, the Articles of Association, SAFE capital registration, the company seal and legal representative's seal, and the identity documents of all natural person controllers. For a Taiwanese parent shareholder, the parent's corporate documents must be notarised by a Taiwan notary and then authenticated by a designated cross-strait agency; a Taiwanese director attending as an individual must present a valid Mainland Travel Permit for Taiwan Residents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanction and trade diversion risk from semiconductor transactions; chip wholesale may feed military or intelligence end-use sectors (dual-use goods).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete product catalogue with ECCN/HTS classification codes for all SSD and CPU items; detailed end-user and end-use certificates from Chinese and Foreign buyers; denied-party screening results against the sanctioned-party list; a compliance letter confirming no re-export to prohibited bodies; and a full import/export transaction list with customs declarations, bills of lading, packing lists and invoice values.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity around the Taiwanese holding company link and cross-strait political uncertainty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarised corporate registry extract and certificate of incorporation of the Taiwan parent; the chain of control from ultimate natural shareholders through each intermediate holding entity; the UBO declaration in the PRC anti-money-laundering format; audited financial statements of the Taiwan parent for the last two years; and a shareholder resolution designating the WFOE's local representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained third-party payments and possible trade-based money laundering through an escrow inspection route.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial contracts, original invoices, arranged escrow agreements and inspection certificates, third-party payment authorisation letters where the counterparty is not the importer/exporter, transaction flow charts connecting all parties, and bank statements evidencing actual movement of funds tied to specific goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin capitalisation or shareholder-loan structure that could facilitate non-arm's-length funds transfer from Taiwan into mainland China.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE foreign debt registration certificate (FSIS/SAFE registration form), board resolutions setting an arm's-length interest rate, loan agreement with repayment schedule, interest withholding tax payment receipts, and an explanation of the commercial rationale for intercompany lending versus equity capital.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For injecting initial paid-in capital from Taiwan to the CN WFOE, the Taiwan shareholder first obtains a capital verification through the issuance of a RMB or foreign exchange capital account after SAFE registration of the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) agreement. The transfer should be executed via SWIFT MT103 using the SAFE FX declaration purpose code applicable to inward direct investment. The remittance instruction must reference the Investment File Number issued by SAFE; the beneficiary is the FX capital account of the WFOE at a designated Tier-1 bank. After arrival, the WFOE instructs the bank to encumber the funds into RMB based on a capital-payment purpose declaration, and a CPA then issues an independent capital verification report confirming the subscribed capital has been fully paid before the commercial registry recordal is updated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade payments for the procurement of SSDs and processors shall be primarily settled through SWIFT MT103 from the WFOE's current foreign exchange account, or through a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) issued by the Chinese bank, using documentary collection (D/P or D/A) for transferable trade. The bank will require a completed Application for Cross-Border Trade Payment, a proforma or final invoice, the sales contract, customs declaration for imports if already cleared, and a bill of lading or air waybill. For RMB settlement with counterparties within China, the clearing rails are through the RMB cross-border interbank payment system (CIPS) or China National Clearing Centre (CNAPS) with actual funds settled via CNAPS. For USD or other foreign-currency payments, the domestic bank will debit a foreign exchange settlement account after verifying the authenticity of the underlying trade; the WFOE is not allowed to pay commission to uninvoiced third parties without evidence of the incentive service, which is a TBML red flag.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Bona fide rolling forward contracts with a domestic designated bank for genuine trade-backed exposure in USD/RMB and EUR/RMB, based on verified underlying contracts.
Cross-currency swaps including interest-rate swaps on eligible external debt service where the principal amount remains outstanding and the derivative transaction is registered with SAFE.

Currency options (both call and put) on offshore or onshore underlying cash flows, but only with the trade or capital account background; NDFs are not permissible for the onshore WFOE, although the Taiwan parent may use offshore NDFs outside mainland jurisdiction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting Resolution together with the statutory financial statement package comprising the business report, financial statements, and profit-appropriation or loss-covering proposal; approved minutes signed and retained in the corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and the Department of Commercial and Industrial, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, where the financial statements exceed the mandatory audit threshold or where registration changes arise from the resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year end; for a calendar-year WFOE, by 30 June; the board must deliver the financial statement package to shareholders at least 30 days before the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For failure to hold the annual shareholders' meeting within the six-month window, the MOEA may issue an order to convene within a supplementary period; non-compliance may expose the responsible officer to fines of TWD 20,000 to TWD 500,000 per occurrence, with continued willful default triggering administrative dissolution, the functional equivalent of strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return, including the completed return, supporting schedules, closing book inventory, and, where the statutory audit threshold is met, the CPA-audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (local office), Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after fiscal year close; for a calendar-year WFOE, by 31 May of the following year, subject to prescribed extension procedures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment penalties accrue at 3% of the unpaid tax for each month or fraction of a month, capped at 30%, plus interest at the postal one-year savings rate; deliberate failure to file or maintain books may lead to estimated assessment, additional penal tax of 10% to 20%, administrative fines of up to TWD 5,000,000, and criminal liability for severe tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Operation and Shareholding Report submitted by the foreign-invested WFOE to the Taiwan Investment Commission, covering current shareholders, beneficial owners, paid-in capital status, operating activity, and financial condition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within six months after fiscal year end; for a calendar-year WFOE, no later than 30 June, unless a shorter period is stated in the investment approval conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false reporting may trigger a rectification order and suspension or revocation of foreign-investment approval privileges, including restriction of dividend remittance, capital repatriation, share transfer approval, and future business licensing applications; repeated non-compliance may lead to cancellation of the foreign investment approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Act Article 22-1 Beneficial Ownership and Shareholder Register Annual Confirmation, filing the current register of directors, supervisors, managers, shareholders holding 10% or more of shares, and ultimate beneficial owners with the MOEA platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commercial and Industrial, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation must be completed no later than 30 June for the previous calendar year, and every shareholding, directorship, managerial, or beneficial-ownership change must be reported within 15 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register or false registration under Company Act Article 22-1 subjects the company to a fine of TWD 50,000 to TWD 500,000, with an additional fine imposed on the responsible officer; continuing default may result in repeated fines and, in severe cases, administrative action against the company's registration status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Registration Change Filing for any annual update or corporate-event filing, including changes in directors, managers, registered office, share transfers, or constitutional documents, plus the retained annual confirmation certificate if issued
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commercial and Industrial, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after any registration-required event; for no-change years, the annual confirmation is completed with the Article 22-1 register by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registration of changes is a legal condition for third-party effectiveness; late filing may expose the company to fines of TWD 1,000 to TWD 5,000, with repeated orders for rectification and, if the company ceases to maintain an effective registration, administrative dissolution by the competent authority.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Taiwan-incorporated WFOE is legally required to appoint an independent Taiwan-certified public accountant (CPA) to audit annual financial statements when the paid-in capital reaches or exceeds TWD 30,000,000 (approximately USD 937,500 at 32 TWD/USD); administrative guidance from the Ministry of Economic Affairs and tax authorities also treats an enterprise as audit-required where total assets exceed TWD 50,000,000 or annual net turnover exceeds TWD 100,000,000, and any company supervised by the Financial Supervisory Commission, public companies, financial institutions, insurance enterprises, and securities firms are always subject to a statutory audit; there is no standalone company-law headcount trigger for a CPA audit, but an enterprise with 100 or more employees becomes subject to separate labor-pension, employee-welfare, and social-insurance audit certifications, while lenders, escrow counterparties, and semiconductor supply-chain principals may contractually require audited financial statements regardless of the statutory threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private Taiwan WFOEs prepare annual financial statements under the Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS), which are substantially converged with the IFRS for SMEs; public or FSC-regulated entities apply Taiwan-IFRS; locally incorporated WFOEs must also satisfy the books-and-records requirements of the Business Entity Accounting Act and compute taxable income under the Income Tax Act, with registered books retained at the principal place of business in Taiwan.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the WFOE must register all directors, supervisors, managers, shareholders holding 10% or more of the outstanding shares, and the ultimate beneficial owners on the MOEA electronic register; any share transfer or beneficial-ownership change triggers a statutory 15-day reporting window, measured from the earlier of the share transfer record date or the board/owner resolution date, and the annual confirmation must be completed by 30 June following the reporting fiscal year; the WFOE must keep the Article 22-1 register reconciled with the shareholder register, transfer ledger, and minutes of shareholders and directors, and the same records must be available on-site for inspection by the MOEA and tax authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners and 10% or More Shareholders

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - 2,200 per year for a Taipei or New Taipei registered office address, company secretary/registered agent, and routine annual registry administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - 18,000 per year for a Taiwan CPA audit of a semiconductor wholesale WFOE, depending on transaction volume, stock counts, intercompany balances, and whether consolidated or group audit procedures are required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% preferential rate for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises; 10% rate for qualified integrated-circuit and software enterprises; effective 5% rate for small low-profit enterprises with annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million; 100% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; possible 15% preferential rate under Hainan Free Trade Port or encouraged-industry policies if the WFOE maintains substantive business and obtains the relevant registration or filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Quarterly Prepayment Return (Form A200000) and Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form A100000) filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic filing system ('e-Tax') and the local competent tax authority portal; supplementary related-party transaction reporting forms (Form A109000 and G100000 series) apply where cross-border related-party transactions exist.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayments must be filed and paid within 15 days after the end of each quarter; the annual final settlement return must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., no later than 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue from sales of goods: gross turnover from wholesale brokerage and resale of solid-state drives (SSDs) and server/CPU chips under ISIC 4651.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter revenue exclusive of VAT and any pass-through customs duties or freight. For a Taiwan-parented WFOE, clearly distinguish the role as a limited-risk distributor, commissionaire, or buy-sell reseller. A commission-only return should be reported if the WFOE lacks title to inventory under the applicable cross-border agency agreement; failing to exclude pass-through receipts creates gross revenue overstatement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales: landed cost of purchased SSDs and CPU chips, including purchase price, freight, insurance, and unrecoverable import costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Match cost with revenue under a consistent inventory costing method. Related-party purchases from the Taiwan parent or Taiwan-manufactured goods must satisfy the arm's length standard; inflated intercompany cost pricing will trigger transfer pricing adjustment under PRC EIT Law Article 41. Import VAT is generally creditable only with valid Special VAT Invoices or customs payment vouchers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit: revenue less cost of sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resulting gross margin should be benchmarked against independent semiconductor wholesale distributors. A persistently thin or negative gross margin while the Taiwan parent retains substantive price, credit, and inventory risk will expose the WFOE to profit reallocation on a transactional net margin method (TNMM) basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses: wages, rent, logistics, compliance, banking, audit, and other operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees charged by the Taiwan parent are deductible only when supported by actual services, contracts, and group allocation documentation. Duplicate head-office charges, shareholder services, or charges disproportionate to the WFOE's local functions will be disallowed. Non-deductible items such as excessive entertainment expenses and tax surcharges must be added back in the tax adjustment schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses: interest and financing costs, bank transfer charges, escrow and SWIFT transaction fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party interest from the Taiwan parent is deductible only to the extent of China's thin capitalization limitation, generally a 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio for non-financial enterprises. Interest exceeding the arm's length range or the statutory debt-to-equity threshold is disallowed and may be recharacterized as a deemed dividend distribution subject to withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating profit: gross profit less operating expenses, financial expenses, and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE performs routine distribution functions while the Taiwan parent bears innovative, demand, and entrepreneurial risks, the routine profit allocable to the Chinese entity should approximate an arm's length return under TNMM or a cost-plus method. Residual profit should remain outside China only when supported by substance and risk-allocation analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and expenses: exchange gains or losses, asset disposals, donations, fines, and foreign shareholder waivers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Debt forgiveness or capital injections from the Taiwan parent may constitute taxable non-operating income or capital reserve depending on legal form. Penalty surcharges and criminal fines are non-deductible. Foreign exchange gains or losses on sourcing from Taiwan must be computed under the PRC Accounting Standards and supported by bank records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total pre-tax profit: book accounting profit before income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This field must reconcile with the statutory financial statements of the WFOE. Any payment to the Taiwan parent not supported by bona fide goods, services, or debt will be treated as a dividend, loan, or capital transaction and may trigger withholding tax, interest, and understatement penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after tax adjustments and loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Start with total pre-tax profit and add back permanently non-deductible expenses, excess related-party interest, and disallowed entertainment or management fees; subtract allowable tax-exempt income and qualifying loss carryforwards. Losses may generally be carried forward 5 years; a 10-year carryforward may apply to qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises or Technology Advanced Service Enterprises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate and calculated corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% statutory rate, or the reduced rate for which the WFOE has obtained or filed the necessary certificate. The 15% High and New Technology Enterprise rate requires six independent intellectual property rights, qualifying R&D expenditure ratios, and a high-technology services income ratio; the 10% IC/software enterprise rate requires a China-incorporated operating entity with relevant registration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, quarterly prepayments, and already-withheld tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quarterly prepayments on Form A200000 are credited here. If the WFOE has Taiwan-source income, a direct or indirect foreign tax credit is available under the EIT Law subject to country-source limitations and the applicable Cross-Strait tax arrangement, but the credit cannot exceed the PRC tax computed on that same foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due or refundable after credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any final tax shortfall must be settled by 31 May. A refund claim is subject to desk audit and the PRC foreign exchange administration outflow controls. Where profits have been distributed to the Taiwan parent, a separate 10% dividend withholding tax declaration is required at the time of distribution, not on this corporate income tax return line.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return attracts a penalty under the PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 62 of RMB 2,000 for ordinary cases and RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious circumstances. Late payment interest accrues daily at 0.05% of the unpaid tax. Under Article 63, tax evasion through false returns, non-disclosure of related-party transactions, or fraudulent treaty claims attracts a monetary penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax and criminal prosecution. Serious non-compliance triggers inclusion on the Serious Dishonest Taxpayer blacklist, resulting in travel bans, restrictions on high consumption, and revocation of certain tax facilitation treatments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 3 and 37 on dividends paid by a PRC resident enterprise to a non-resident beneficial owner; where the applicable Cross-Strait Taxation Arrangement is administratively effective and the Taiwan-resident shareholder meets the conditions, a reduced 5% rate may apply to dividends if the beneficial owner holds directly at least 25% of the WFOE's capital for a continuous 12-month period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA or Cross-Strait Arrangement relief, the Taiwan-resident shareholder must submit an application for treaty entitlement through the PRC withholding agent under the State Taxation Administration Announcement 2015 No. 60 and 2019 No. 35. The application package must include: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Taiwan competent tax authority; (ii) a beneficial ownership self-declaration supported by substantive business evidence; (iii) ownership records proving the 25% shareholding and 12-month holding period; (iv) board resolutions and distribution vouchers; and (v) any additional materials requested by the local PRC tax authority. The tax authority may issue an advance confirmation or apply the treaty rate after review. If the claim is rejected ex post, the WFOE as withholding agent is liable for the under-withheld tax, late payment surcharge, and penalties; a shell or conduit shareholder will be denied relief under the general anti-abuse rule.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest paid by a PRC enterprise to a Taiwan non-resident is 10% each. Under the Cross-Strait Taxation Arrangement, where effective and properly claimed, the rate may be reduced to 7% for interest and 7% for royalties, subject to beneficial ownership and substance requirements. Related-party interest must also satisfy China's thin capitalization and arm's length financing requirements; royalties must be associated with genuine intellectual property transfers or licensing and not disguised service or management fees.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 200 million aggregate annual related-party tangible property transactions for mandatory Local File preparation; RMB 100 million for related-party intangible property or financial asset transfers; RMB 40 million for related-party service transactions. The annual related-party transaction declaration applies separately, and the Master File / CbCR thresholds may trigger at group consolidated revenue of RMB 2 billion / RMB 5.5 billion respectively.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mainland China does not apply Gulf Cooperation Council-style Economic Substance Regulations, but PRC tax law applies substance-over-form, beneficial ownership, and reasonable commercial purpose doctrines. The Taiwan-parented WFOE must demonstrate that it employs substantive local staff, maintains decision-making authority and physical premises in China, bears meaningful wholesale inventory and customer-credit risk, and performs the core income-generating activities (CIGA) associated with SSD and CPU distribution. A passive or paper WFOE with no local business reality and no economic substance will be treated as a conduit or shell for treaty and GAAR purposes, with transactions recharacterized and profit reallocated to the ultimate economic owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Profit Shifting / Missing Contemporaneous Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE systematically purchases SSD and CPU chips from the Taiwan parent at inflated prices, operates at artificially thin or negative gross margins, fails to prepare a Local File or Master File when related-party transactions exceed the statutory thresholds, and provides no benchmark or risk-allocation analysis to support the intercompany pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 41 and Article 44, the competent tax authority may make a special tax adjustment to the WFOE's taxable income, impute an arm's length profit, and levy interest plus a 5% late-payment surcharge on the adjusted tax. Under the Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 63, intentional understatement of taxable income attracts a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax and criminal liability where the amount is significant.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: directors and the legal representative may be held jointly and severally liable for the entity's tax shortfall where they directed or knowingly benefited from the pricing scheme. They may be placed on the Serious Dishonest Taxpayer blacklist, triggering exit bans and restrictions on high consumption, and may face criminal prosecution under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 with imprisonment of up to 7 years for serious tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion Through Artificial Recharacterization of Dividends as Fees, Interest, or Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE distributes profits to the Taiwan parent disguised as management service fees, non-arm's-length interest on shareholder loans, or fictitious royalty payments to avoid the 10% dividend withholding tax, and then claims treaty or Cross-Strait Arrangement benefits using a shell conduit with no beneficial ownership substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PRC tax authority has the power to recharacterize the payments as dividends under the general anti-avoidance rule in Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 and the special anti-abuse rules for treaty benefits under State Taxation Administration Announcement 2015 No. 60. The WFOE, as withholding agent, will be ordered to pay the under-withheld 10% withholding tax, daily surcharges, and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded; fraudulent TRC or beneficial-ownership filings carry debtor's imprisonment risk under Criminal Law Articles 201 and 205.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: directors who approved false agreements, fabricated invoices, or directed the round-tripping of funds face personal civil restitution, a travel ban, blacklisting by the tax administration, and criminal liability as principals under PRC Criminal Law Article 201. If foreign-exchange controls are circumvented, additional liability under the State Administration of Foreign Exchange anti-money-laundering regime may include asset freezing and personal fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Structure, False VAT Invoicing, and Money Laundering in Semiconductor Trade
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a shell WFOE with no employees, warehouse, or physical management, while issuing or obtaining false Special VAT Invoices to inflate SSD/CPU costs, creating fake export orders, routing funds through multiple shell accounts, or conducting 'round-trip' capital flows to fabricate economic activity and manipulate tax and customs outcomes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Issuing false Special VAT Invoices violates PRC Criminal Law Article 205 and is punishable, in serious cases, by life imprisonment and property forfeiture. The tax authority will impose monetary penalties, deny VAT deduction and export refunds, disallow all related deductions, and assess corporate income tax plus late-payment surcharge and penalties. Under the AML framework, the suspicious Swift/TT and escrow payments may be reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit, triggering account freezing and forfeiture proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: directors and beneficial owners who forged trade documents, controlled shell bank accounts, or directed the false invoicing scheme are personally liable for restitution of the tax and customs duties defrauded. They face criminal imprisonment, travel bans, entry restrictions on cross-strait movement, blacklisting as seriously dishonest persons, and joint and several civil liability to creditors, the tax authority, and the customs authority.
